artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $S$ denote the class of functions $f$ that are analytic and univalent (one-to-one) on $\mathbb{D}$ with $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. It is classical that for every $f\in S$ and every $z_0\in\mathbb{D}$, writing $\rho=|z_0|$,
$$\left|\frac{f''(z_0)}{f'(z_0)}-\frac{2\bar{z_0}}{1-\rho^2}\right|\le\frac{4}{1-\rho^2}.$$
Now restrict attention to the subclass $S_{\mathbb{R}}\subset S$ consisting of those $f\in S$ whose Taylor coefficients at $0$ are all real (equivalently, $f$ takes real values on $\mathbb{D}\cap\mathbb{R}$).

Determine whether the above inequality can be strengthened for $f\in S_{\mathbb{R}}$: that is, find the sharp upper bound, as a function of $z_0\in\mathbb{D}$, of
$$\left|\frac{f''(z_0)}{f'(z_0)}-\frac{2\bar{z_0}}{1-|z_0|^2}\right|$$
over $f\in S_{\mathbb{R}}$, and determine the extremal functions.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for improvements to the classical Hayman-type pre-Schwarzian-like inequality for univalent functions with real coefficients did not return any source addressing Sundberg's specific question. No paper claiming a sharp improved bound for the class $S_{\mathbb{R}}$ was located, and the problem appears to remain open or at least unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Locally Univalent Functions on the Unit Disk
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses classical pre-Schwarzian estimates for univalent functions but does not address the real-coefficient refinement.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references contain the classical bound 4/(1-|z|^2) but no sharper analogue for real-coefficient univalent functions.

status_evidence.title: Norm Estimates of the Pre-Schwarzian Derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper on pre-Schwarzian norm estimates for various subclasses, none specifically the class S_R of univalent functions with real coefficients addressing Sundberg's question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on pre-Schwarzian estimates does not appear to resolve Sundberg's question.
